title: Typed invocation bridge and ergonomic streaming/retry helpers for SDKs
creator: Ava Morgan
description:
Goal: deliver a cross-language "typed invocation bridge" and a set of ergonomic helpers that make function/tool calling in Redwood SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) safe, discoverable, and resilient for streaming/long-running operations. This work targets three developer pain points observed in internal support tickets and customer feedback: 1) brittle runtime-only schema validation that surfaces errors far from call sites; 2) poor streaming ergonomics when callers need to resume partial results or retry mid-stream; 3) inconsistent retry semantics for functions that cause side effects or are not idempotent.

Approach: implement a hybrid validation model where we generate lightweight validators at package build time (TS: codegen + types, Python: optional pydantic model generator, Go: go generate -> validator funcs) and keep a small runtime guard to catch schema drift. Add an "invocation bridge" utility that: canonicalizes incoming function schemas to a normalized form, exposes typed client helpers per-language, and wires idempotency tokens + checkpoint markers for streaming calls. Provide a unified retry policy object that is streaming-aware (can checkpoint and resume at the last processed event) and supports a side-effect policy flag (no-side-effects / safe-retry / at-most-once via coordinator).

Why hybrid: compile-time/generated validators improve DX by surfacing type errors earlier and giving editors autocompletion. Pure compile-time is infeasible for dynamic models and remote schema updates; a small runtime guard ensures we fail fast on drift. The streaming-aware retry design trades additional metadata (checkpoint headers, small sequence ids) for dramatically reduced duplicated work on retries for long streams.

Out of scope for this ticket: full autopatching of customer function specs; protocol-level streaming protocol (we reuse existing runtime streaming envelope), and advanced distributed checkpointing (future work).
acceptance_criteria: Generator produces language-native validators for given function schema and integrates with SDK packaging (ts: .d.ts + validator, py: optional generated pydantic model, go: validator funcs)
Invocation bridge API exported in js/ts/python/go SDKs with consistent naming and migration doc
Streaming helper supports checkpoints and resume semantics with integration tests that simulate transient network failures and retries
Retry policy supports a side-effect safety flag and is documented; default policy is conservative (no unsafe retries for non-idempotent calls unless caller opts in)
Benchmark: runtime overhead <= 6% median p50 for small functions compared to current baseline; functional correctness verified against existing function-calling fixtures
Public example apps in SDK repo showing async iterator (ts), async generator (py), and channel-based (go) consumption patterns
comments: 2025-02-16 - Ava Morgan: Kickoff spike completed. Prototype generator for TypeScript that emits a lightweight runtime validator + declaration file. Found two real-world schemas that rely on additionalProperties: we decided to keep canonical form with explicit 'open' flag to avoid losing consumer flexibility.

2025-02-19 - Diego Ramirez: Pushed initial TypeScript prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1289. The PR wires a new 'invocationBridge' export and a 'createValidator' codegen step. Bench micro results: cold build adds ~25KB to bundle, runtime validate adds ~3-5% CPU for small prompt-only functions.

2025-02-21 - Code review (L. Chen): raised concern about generator running during user installs (cost). Decision: generator runs at dev/build time; we provide a fallback runtime validator shipped in SDK for users who don't pre-generate (smaller feature set).

2025-02-27 - UX review (Maya Patel): requested higher-level helper for TS that returns AsyncIterable<ResultChunk> and hides checkpoint headers. Added a small 'autoResume' boolean and 'onCheckpoint' callback for advanced usage.

2025-03-01 - Integration tests added (Diego): added test suite that simulates an intermittent network disconnect midway through a stream and verifies resume semantics. All tests pass in local CI. Test PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1310
2025-03-02 - PM feedback (Nora Singh): ensure examples include a migration guide for existing function-calling users. I updated the docs draft and linked it in attachments.
2025-03-03 - Security review requested: added ticket to review idempotency token generation and replay risk. See dependency ENG-54219 for related KMS design notes.

2025-03-04 - Diego Ramirez: Addressed TS typing edge-cases (union return types) and tightened runtime guard to strip unknown fields when schema has 'closed' flag. Preparing for internal beta in sdk-2025.03 release branch.
